steps.check: The dashboard is in the sidebar. Its list matches Settings → Automations side by side, in the light and the dark theme.
Pause 15 min from the card: the automation is off, the sensor lists it, the countdown runs.
The end of the timer turns the automation on (reason timer).
steps.note: On time to 10 ms. The logbook stays empty on that system because its recorder excludes the automation domain.

steps.check: Pause again while paused: new end time, the start time stays, one entry.
Resume now turns the automation on at once.
A manual turn-on ends the pause. The old timer does not turn the automation on later.
Restart during a pause: the automation stays off, the countdown continues.
steps.note: The timer fired on time after the restart.

steps.check: The end time passes while Home Assistant is down: the automation resumes at startup.
Reload of a changed automation during a pause: the pause stays.
Automation without id: a clear error, nothing changes.
steps.note: The REST API reports HTTP 500 for a validation error. The websocket path that the card uses returns the translated message.

steps.check: Search narrows the list. Sort by last run puts the newest first. A new automation appears with no configuration.
Dashboard edits survive an integration reload. Rebuild the dashboard resets them.
Phone width: no horizontal scroll, the chips are easy to tap.
Closing the pause dialog raises no error in Home Assistant.
steps.note: A TypeError in Home Assistant's quick bar: the card's internal event had Home Assistant's name dialog-closed. Fixed in the next release: the card's internal events have the prefix automation-pause-.

steps.check: Update from 0.1.0-beta.1 through HACS and restart: the pauses stay.
steps.note: A pause made before the update was still there after the restart, with its end time.

steps.check: An existing install keeps its sensor entity ID; the sensor gets the service device.
steps.note: The entity ID stayed the same; the name now starts with the device name.

steps.check: With Notify when a pause ends: the timer end shows a notification.
steps.note: The notification appeared at the same second as the turn-on.

steps.check: Closing the pause dialog raises no error in Home Assistant.
steps.note: One error was logged after the update. Its position matches the 0.1.0-beta.1 card: a browser tab open since before the update still ran the old code. Check again after a reload.

steps.check: Admin only hides the dashboard from users who are not administrators.
The list shows each automation's own icon.
The dashboard is in the sidebar. Its list matches Settings → Automations side by side, in the light and the dark theme.
Search narrows the list. Sort by last run puts the newest first. A new automation appears with no configuration.
Phone width: no horizontal scroll, the chips are easy to tap.
Update from 0.1.0-beta.3 through HACS and restart: the pauses and options stay.
steps.note: Three pauses and the configured durations were unchanged after the restart.

steps.check: The frontend imports the loader, and the loader loads the card.
steps.note: The page imports the loader with the version query. No load failure was logged.

steps.check: The dashboard works in the Android Companion app.
steps.note: Failed with 0.1.0-beta.2 and 0.1.0-beta.3 (Custom element doesn't exist), also after a reset of the frontend cache. Works with 0.1.0-beta.4.

steps.check: The dashboard works in Chrome on a phone.
The dashboard follows a card-mod theme (Frosted Glass): background image and glass card.
The dashboard is in the sidebar. Its list matches Settings → Automations side by side, in the light and the dark theme.
Search narrows the list. Sort by last run puts the newest first. A new automation appears with no configuration.
Phone width: no horizontal scroll, the chips are easy to tap.
